bullets.text: The US has announced new tariffs on several of its largest trading partners, including China and the EU, signalling a shift in global trade policies.
New images reveal a stadium-sized crater on an asteroid, four years after a spacecraft deliberately crashed into it as part of a test of Earth's planetary defence systems.
Judges in Israel have recommended dropping the most serious charges against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, with little chance of conviction in one of his three ongoing cases.
South Australian Liberal senator Leah Blyth has defected to One Nation, citing a loss of confidence in the Liberal party's direction.
An out-of-control bushfire on Flinders Island has burned approximately 13,000 hectares, with fire services warning of its rapid south-west movement.
Gold Coast Mayor Tom Tate reportedly secured a lucrative deal for a prime real estate parcel, taking over the private purchase from a major Australian developer.
US stocks experienced a volatile session, with AI-related companies like Nvidia facing pressure, although AI start-up Anthropic saw its shares recover above IPO price.
The US Treasury's financial crime watchdog, FinCen, was hit by a suspected cyber attack, leading to systems being taken offline amidst growing concerns over technology system vulnerabilities.

US GDP figures were upgraded, with the economy growing at an annualised rate of 4.3% in the third quarter, up from an initial estimate of 3.4%, which could keep a December rate rise in play for the Federal Reserve.
